chunks: And it has been narrated to me via the path of Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi (may Allah be pleased with him) regarding that matter something strange.

And it is that he narrated that Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: 'Nothing appeared to Allah as an appearance (Bada') as what appeared to Him regarding my father Isma'il, when He commanded his father Ibrahim to slaughter him, then He ransomed him with a great sacrifice.'
And in the hadith, regarding both meanings, I have my consideration, except that I have included it for the meaning of the word 'Bada'', and Allah is the Director to the correctness.

key_terms.الْبَدَاءُ: Bada' (Divine appearance/revelation of a new decree or change in divine plan)

ai.seo_question: What is the concept of Al-Bada' in Shia theology as illustrated by the story of Ibrahim and Isma'il?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this unique narration from Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi to illustrate 'Al-Bada'' as a divine manifestation of a new decree, specifically citing the near-slaughter of Isma'il (AS) and its subsequent ransom. Although he acknowledges scholarly nuance regarding the exact nature of this event, he includes it to highlight the linguistic and theological depth of the term, affirming that God's knowledge and will can manifest in ways that appear as changes to creation. This reflects the Shia view of 'Al-Bada'' not as a change in God's essence, but as a revelation of His decree in accordance with wisdom and circumstances.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 11. The following astonishing tradition has been related to me on the authority of Abu allHusayn al-Asadi (RA)
that Al-Sadiq (AS) said: “Nothing appeared to Allah as regards to my father Isma`il (AS) when He ordered His father Ibrahim (AS) to slaughter him, but He ransomed him with a momentous sacrifice.”

The Compiler of his book says: In this tradition with both its meanings, I have my consideration. However, I have transmitted them here for the meaning of the word `appearance’ [bada’]. Allah is the Director to the correctness.
